summary: Orphaned prefix-cache credits and invoice variance after mixed-queue batch embedding
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports invoice variance for March billing period driven by a large batch-embedding job that ran 2026-03-03 02:00-03:30 UTC. The billing lines show an unexpected credit line labeled 'prefix-cache-savings' but the net invoice total is still higher than expected. Streamlytics believes some cache credits were not applied to the customer account and may have been attributed to the system account during a concurrent cache invalidation window.

Impact:
- Customer sees $2,180 higher charge on March invoice than forecasted.
- Affects downstream cost forecasting for their analytics product; they are on a dedicated contract and expect predictable monthly usage.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-3 (GPU A100), batch-queue: mixed-small, autoscaler: enabled
- API keys: redacted in logs (shared via secure channel)

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) Customer submitted multi-tenant batch-embed job (200k documents) using mixed queue at 2026-03-03T02:00Z.
2) At ~02:18Z an automated global prefix-cache invalidation ran as part of a scheduled rollout (runtime deployment 2026-03-03-02a).
3) Between 02:18Z-02:22Z we observed elevated retry rates and a cluster of short-lived job restarts for the batch-embed controller.
4) Metering pipeline shows a burst of "cache_hit" credits generated but later a subset of those credits lack customer account IDs and appear with system org id in the metering ledger.
5) Invoice generation job aggregated totals and created a credit line but did not reassign orphaned credits to the customer's invoice.

Logs / Links:
- Billing ledger window (redacted): https://billing.redwood.ai/ledgers/2026-03-03/window-02
- Runtime deploy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/1f2b3c4
- Support slack thread: #support-streamlytics (link shared in secure channel)

Requested outcome:
- Clear audit showing which credits were orphaned and why.
- If credits belong to the customer, apply retroactive credit and reissue corrected invoice or provide a credit memo.
- Root cause and mitigation to prevent misattribution during small rollout/cache-invalidation windows.

investigation_notes: Metering pipeline trace shows worker instance w-77d had missing org header during write to ledger due to transient failure while reloading secrets (observed 02:18:21Z).
Cache invalidation event triggered a windowed flush that caused the batch controller to requeue tasks; requeued tasks reused ephemeral worker tokens that were not fully hydrated with org metadata.
Ledger schema allows null org_id but downstream invoice aggregator assumes non-null and treats null as system-org causing credits to appear in system bucket.

Backfill heuristic: match orphaned credit records by (job_id, timestamp range, model, token_count) to customer job. Precision currently 91% for this window. Remaining records require manual correlation with worker logs.
Hotfix deployed: metering-worker now performs a pre-write validation ensuring org_id present; if missing it retries secret hydration up to 3x and emits an alert to #ops-metering if still missing.
Longer-term fix: add strict transactional propagation of org metadata through requeue/retry path and add unit tests for secret hydration during concurrent cache invalidation events.
resolution_summary: In progress: hotfix deployed to prevent new orphaned credits; backfill and reconciliation identified the majority of orphaned credits and billing will issue a credit memo for matched amount. Manual review remains for a small residual set. Final invoice adjustment and post-incident review pending.
